claim_samples.caveat: User-defined target; 0.4/day and 20 hours/machine are derived scheduling metrics, not build labor or current capacity.
claim_samples.escalation: Define product acceptance envelope and validate takt, WIP, rework, and qualification-cell assumptions.
claim_samples.subject: 100 high-quality CNC machining centers/year
claim_samples.text: A target of 100 machines per year is approximately two machines per production week, or 0.4 finished machines per working day under a 250-day calendar. A simple takt calculation gives 20 available working hours per completed machine, but this is a **DERIVED scheduling metric**, not the build labor content. Final assembly, wiring, alignment, calibration, test cutting, rework, documentation, and customer acceptance do not happen in one 20-hour operation; they overlap through a cell-based flow. A reasonable first design is therefore a low-volume, high-control factory with parallel structural preparation, subsystem integration, assembly, calibration, and acceptance cells rather than a single conveyor line.

claim_samples.caveat: Official infrastructure supports facility/equipment existence; press capacity is secondary and not independently measured qualified machine throughput.
claim_samples.escalation: Audit BFW operating output, foundry yield, mother-machine utilization, and high-end product qualification.
claim_samples.source_class: Official facility page plus reported secondary press
claim_samples.subject: BFW Hosur foundry and mother-machine infrastructure
claim_samples.text: BFW’s official infrastructure page documents an integrated Hosur foundry, a declared output of up to 600 tonnes per month of grey iron, SG iron, and NiHard castings, and mother-machine equipment including a Mitsubishi 5-face piano miller, Nissan horizontal boring machine, SIP vertical jig boring machine, and Waldrich Coburg slideway grinder. It also documents large-part CMM capability and a spindle excellence center with controlled assembly and testing.[6] A separate 2024 press report described a new Hosur plant with two 20,000-square-metre assembly halls and reported capacity above 10,000 CNC machines per year; this is treated as **REPORTED**, not independently measured qualified capacity.[29]

claim_samples.caveat: Aggregate builder capacity is not a proxy for machines passing a defined simultaneous 5-axis acceptance protocol.
claim_samples.escalation: Collect product-family output, customer acceptance, export, reliability, and test-cell records by year.
claim_samples.subject: India qualified simultaneous 5-axis throughput
claim_samples.text: | Qualified 5-axis throughput | **UNKNOWN.** Aggregate machine capacity does not identify the number of simultaneous 5-axis machines that pass a defined acceptance protocol. | Do not use aggregate plant numbers as proof of high-end production capacity. |

claim_samples.caveat: Thermal and vibratory routes are alternatives requiring geometry, residual-stress, stability, and process validation; no universal duration is promoted.
claim_samples.escalation: Run controlled route comparison with dimensional-drift and residual-stress records.
claim_samples.subject: casting stress-relief route
claim_samples.text: Natural aging of castings for six to twelve months is sometimes used in industry, but the exact duration and necessity are design- and process-dependent. It should be treated as an **ASSUMPTION or DERIVED process option**, not a universal requirement. Thermal stress relief, controlled machining sequence, rib geometry, casting process, and post-machining stabilization can be combined differently. Vibratory stress relief may be useful for certain fabrications, but its sufficiency relative to thermal treatment for a particular high-precision casting is **CONFLICTED** and must be validated experimentally.

capacity_claims.capacity_guard: Aggregate/nameplate/future-plan, product dimensions, orders, and facility existence are not promoted to qualified effective capacity.

claims.claim_counting_note: Layer counts intentionally retain evidence/unknown/conflict overlap; no unproven synthesis is collapsed into a canonical claim.

conflict_samples.conflict: Indian builders report thousands of machines per year, while industry commentary describes high-end core imports and limited domestic precision components.
conflict_samples.resolution: Treat aggregate capacity as valid only for aggregate scope; high-quality 5-axis capacity remains **UNKNOWN**.

conflict_samples.conflict: “Indigenous” or “Made in India” can mean design/assembly, domestic structural content, or deep component manufacture.
conflict_samples.resolution: Report localization by subsystem and do not use a single domestic-value percentage without an audited BOM.

conflict_samples.conflict: BFW Hosur capacity appears as 10,000+ units in press coverage while the official infrastructure page emphasizes foundry and mother-machine capabilities, not a verified annual output.
conflict_samples.resolution: Mark 10,000+ as **REPORTED secondary**; use official BFW page for facility capability, not capacity.

conflict_samples.conflict: THK India has a Sri City production facility, but public evidence does not reveal which product grades and volumes are made there.
conflict_samples.resolution: Mark facility existence as evidenced; grade mix and qualified CNC capacity **UNKNOWN**.

conflict_samples.conflict: MTAR claims sole Indian ball-screw manufacturing, but that does not prove volume production of the specific grades and service lives required by a 100-machine CNC program.
conflict_samples.resolution: Preserve the claim as company-reported capability; mark capacity and qualification **UNKNOWN**.
